facts.fact_text: The main meeting place of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the protest rallies was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
On 22 February 2008 the applicant made a speech at the rally held at Freedom Square.
On 22 February 2008, the same date as the applicant's speech at Freedom Square, the General Prosecutor applied to the President of Armenia seeking to have the applicant dismissed.
On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree dismissing the applicant from the post of Deputy General Prosecutor.
On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree depriving the applicant of his rank of First Category State Justice Councillor.

According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the PDFOC on suspicion of illegal possession, carrying and transportation of arms and ammunition, and for showing resistance to police officers.

The record of the applicant's arrest stated that the applicant was arrested on suspicion of illegal acquisition, possession and carrying of arms and ammunition, as provided for by Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 26 February 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (illegal acquisition, possession or carrying of arms and ammunition).
On 26 February 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (non-life or health-threatening assault on a public official).
On 27 February 2008 at 3.30 a.m. the applicant was brought before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan decided to allow the investigator's application for the applicant's detention.
On 7 March 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the detention decision.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found on 7 March 2008 that there was a reasonable suspicion, from the materials submitted, that the applicant had committed the imputed offences.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found on 7 March 2008 that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's decision to detain the applicant was well-reasoned.
On 18 April 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan extended the applicant's detention by two months.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found on 18 April 2008 that, if the applicant remained at large, he could abscond or obstruct the investigation by exerting unlawful pressure on the persons involved in the proceedings, concealing or falsifying materials essential for the case or in some other way.

On 23 April 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal against the extension of his detention, arguing inter alia that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's decision was unreasoned and the risks of his absconding or obstructing the investigation were unsubstantiated.

On 8 May 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the extension of his detention, finding that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's decision to extend the applicant's detention was well-reasoned.
On 6 June 2008 the investigator questioned the applicant, in the main asking him to explain the speech he had made at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008.

On 13 June 2008 the charge of illegal possession of a weapon under Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code was dropped on the ground that the applicant had a licence to keep and carry the Browning pistol.

On 13 June 2008 the charge of illegal possession of a weapon under Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code was dropped on the ground that it had not been possible to establish the circumstances under which the extra digit had been added to the Browning pistol's serial number.
On 13 June 2008 a new charge was brought against the applicant under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (usurpation of power).

The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant, following the 19 February 2008 presidential election, had joined Levon Ter-Petrosyan and his followers in masterminding and taking actions seeking to usurp power.

The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant, using his standing as Deputy General Prosecutor, had participated in discrediting the conduct of the election, casting doubt on its lawfulness among the international community, and instilling distrust towards the results among large segments of the population.

The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant had created illusions of public discontent and revolt, and organised and conducted unlawful mass rallies aimed at destabilising the political situation in Armenia.

The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant had planned and taken actions seeking to isolate lawful public officials, force them to resign and exercise power in their stead.
The new charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code alleged that the applicant had made public speeches and calls of a provocative nature aimed at usurping state power.

On 13 June 2008 the investigator requested that the applicant's detention be extended, taking into account inter alia the fact that it was a voluminous and complex criminal case which required further numerous investigative measures.

The investigator's request for extension of the applicant's detention on 13 June 2008 noted that, beside the applicant, a number of other individuals were accused under Article 300 of the Armenian Criminal Code, including some who were in hiding.
On 19 June 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan extended the applicant's detention by two more months.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, in extending the applicant's detention on 19 June 2008, took into account the nature and gravity of the imputed offences.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found on 19 June 2008 that, if the applicant remained at large, he could abscond, obstruct the proceedings by exerting pressure on the persons involved in the proceedings and, by his actions, hinder the further disclosure of the circumstances of the case.
On 23 June 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal arguing inter alia that his detention was not based on a reasonable suspicion.

In his appeal of 23 June 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had failed to provide any reasons in support of its finding that he might abscond or obstruct the proceedings.
On 2 July 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the extension of his detention.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found on 2 July 2008 that there was a reasonable suspicion from the materials submitted that the applicant had committed an offence.
The Criminal Court of Appeal found on 2 July 2008 that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan's decision to extend the applicant's detention was well-reasoned.
On 13 August 2008 the charge of usurpation of power under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code was dropped for lack of sufficient evidence.
It was stated on 13 August 2008 that numerous investigative measures had been taken but no new evidence of the applicant's participation in usurpation of state power had been obtained.
On 13 August 2008 the applicant's criminal case was disjoined from case number 62202608.
On 22 August 2008 the investigation into the applicant's criminal case was completed and the case was referred to the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan for trial.
On 22 August 2008 Judge Z.V. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan decided to take over the applicant's criminal case and to set the case down for trial.
On 22 August 2008 Judge Z.V. ruled that the applicant's preventive measure was to remain unchanged.
On 1 September 2008 Judge Z.V. examined a challenge lodged by the applicant seeking that the judge recuse himself from the examination of the case for lack of impartiality.

The applicant's challenge for recusal of Judge Z.V. was based on the fact that the judge's son, A.V., who worked as an investigator, was a member of the investigative team entrusted with the investigation of the applicant's case.
Judge Z.V. noted that he was aware that his son A.V. had been a member of the relevant investigative team.
Judge Z.V. found that his son A.V. had not performed or taken part in any investigative measure carried out in respect of the applicant during the investigation of the case.

Judge Z.V. found that he could still conduct an impartial examination since the fact that his son A.V. was a member of the investigative team did not in itself give rise to a reasonable doubt as regards his impartiality.
On 11 February 2009 Judge Z.V. examined and dismissed a request lodged by the applicant seeking to be released, finding that it was still necessary to keep the applicant in detention.
During the trial the applicant pleaded not guilty and submitted that he had not put up any resistance during the police operation.
During the trial the applicant submitted that, having arrived at the courtyard of the PDFOC building, he had seen around 200 to 300 people gathered there.
During the trial the applicant submitted that he had got out of the car and, together with the persons accompanying him, entered the PDFOC building.

During the trial the applicant submitted that his arrest had been effected by ten masked persons who had attacked him and his brother V.J. and subjected them to ill-treatment both at the time of arrest and in the lobby of the PDFOC building.

Police officer A.H. testified that on 23 February 2008 at about 11.30 p.m., while at work, he had received an instruction to accompany an arrested person from the courtyard into the lobby of the PDFOC building and to hand him over to the officers of the criminal intelligence unit.
Police officer A.H. testified that the same instruction had been given to his colleague, officer T.A.
Police officer A.H. testified that as officer T.A. opened the van door, they had recognised the applicant and requested that he step out of the vehicle.

Police officer A.H. testified that the applicant had disobeyed and tried to kick them but they had managed to take him out forcibly and, holding him by the arms, had walked towards the PDFOC building.
Police officer A.H. testified that the applicant had managed to free his right hand and punch officer A.H. in the shoulder, as a result of which officer A.H. had lost his balance and fallen down.

Police officer A.H. testified that as officer T.A. intervened, the applicant, while making threats and swearing at them and their family members, had pulled and torn a pocket on officer T.A.'s uniform.
Police officer A.H. testified that they had then taken the applicant inside the PDFOC building by forcibly twisting his arms, and handed him over to the officers of the criminal intelligence unit.
Police officer T.A. gave testimony similar to that of police officer A.H. regarding the events at the PDFOC on 23 February 2008.
A number of other PDFOC officers testified in court during the applicant's trial.
Seven PDFOC officers stated in court that the applicant had used swear words and made threats in the lobby of the PDFOC.
Fourteen PDFOC officers who had overseen and/or participated in the police operation near Argavand village, including G.G., A.M. and R.M., described the circumstances of that operation in court.

The fourteen PDFOC officers who described the police operation near Argavand village stated inter alia that after arriving at the PDFOC they had been greeted by officers A.H. and T.A., and had immediately entered the building to report the incident.
The applicant requested that four Members of Parliament, Z.P., A.I., A.Sak. and A.D., be summoned as witnesses during the trial.

The applicant claimed that the four Members of Parliament Z.P., A.I., A.Sak. and A.D. had visited him in the remand prison on 27 February 2008 and witnessed his bodily injuries sustained as a result of ill-treatment in police custody.
The applicant requested that three opposition supporters, S.A., V.K. and A.Sis., be summoned as witnesses during the trial.

The applicant argued that S.A., V.K. and A.Sis. had also been taken and kept at the PDFOC on 24 February 2008 and allegedly possessed certain information regarding what had happened there the day before.

The applicant argued that S.A., V.K. and A.Sis. had allegedly been told by police officers that the applicant and his brother V.J. had been beaten on 23 February 2008 and had overheard police officers discussing the case as being 'trumped up' against the applicant.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's requests to summon the witnesses Z.P., A.I., A.Sak., A.D., S.A., V.K. and A.Sis.
On 23 March 2009 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, sitting in a single judge formation composed of Judge Z.V., found the applicant guilty as charged.
On 23 March 2009 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant to three years' imprisonment.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that on 23 February 2008 at around 11.30 p.m. the applicant, having been brought in to the courtyard of the PDFOC upon a suspicion of carrying illegal firearms and ammunition, disobeyed the lawful orders of police officers who were performing their official duties.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant punched and caused pain to police officer A.H.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant pulled and tore the uniform of officer T.A., refused to enter the PDFOC building and threatened the police officers and their families with physical retribution.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant had voluntarily given up his CZ-75 B-type pistol during the police operation near Argavand village.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that all the weapons retrieved during the police operation near Argavand village, including those belonging to the applicant, had been found, following an inspection, to have been possessed and carried legally.
In reaching its findings, the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan relied on the statements of police officers A.H. and T.A. and other officers who had testified in court.
As material evidence, the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan cited officer T.A.'s torn uniform.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant's submissions and arguments to be unsubstantiated.

On 16 April 2009 the applicant lodged an appeal against the District Court's judgment, arguing inter alia that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had failed to assess properly the evidence, dismissed his submissions and refused his requests seeking to prove his innocence.
In his appeal of 16 April 2009, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had based its findings solely on the testimony of the police officers.

In his appeal of 16 April 2009, the applicant alleged that the true reason for his prosecution and conviction was to punish him for the speech he had made at the opposition rally on 22 February 2008, arguing that he had thereby been discriminated against on the basis of his political views.
In his appeal of 16 April 2009, the applicant argued that Judge Z.V. had not been impartial because of the involvement of his son A.V. in the investigative team.

On 20 May 2009 the Court of Appeal upheld the judgment of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan and dismissed the applicant's appeal, finding that the arguments contained therein were unfounded.
On 19 June 2009 the applicant lodged an appeal on points of law to the Court of Cassation.
On 14 July 2009 the Court of Cassation declared the applicant's appeal on points of law inadmissible for lack of merit.
On 22 June 2009 the applicant was released under amnesty.

Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (2003), as in force at the material time, provided that usurpation of State power, namely actions aimed at violent seizure of State power or its violent retention in violation of the Constitution, as well as violent overthrow of the constitutional order of Armenia or violent breach of the territorial integrity of Armenia, was punishable by imprisonment for a period from ten to fifteen years.
On 1 March 2008 in the early morning a police operation was conducted on Freedom Square where several hundred demonstrators were camping.
As a result of the police operation on Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, Freedom Square was cleared of all demonstrators, resulting in clashes between the demonstrators and the police.

On 1 March 2008 criminal proceedings were instituted regarding the events at Freedom Square on the grounds that the leaders of the opposition and their supporters had organised unlawful demonstrations, incited disobedience and committed violence against the police.
Further details of the criminal proceedings instituted on 1 March 2008 regarding the events at Freedom Square are described in Mushegh Saghatelyan v. Armenia, no. 23086/08, § 15, 20 September 2018.
Later on 1 March 2008 the situation in Yerevan deteriorated and rallies continued in a number of streets until the early morning of 2 March 2008.
The rallies continuing on 1-2 March 2008 involved clashes between protesters and law enforcement officers.
The clashes on 1-2 March 2008 resulted in ten deaths, including eight civilians.
The clashes on 1-2 March 2008 resulted in numerous injured persons.
Following the clashes on 1-2 March 2008, a state of emergency was declared by the President of Armenia.

On 2 March 2008 another set of criminal proceedings was instituted on the grounds that the leaders of the opposition and their supporters had organised mass disorder in the streets of Yerevan, including murders, violence and other reprehensible acts.
Further details of the criminal proceedings instituted on 2 March 2008 are described in Mushegh Saghatelyan v. Armenia, no. 23086/08, § 17.
On 2 March 2008 both sets of criminal proceedings instituted on 1 March 2008 and 2 March 2008 were joined and examined under case number 62202608.
